_doc: A2.9/A2.9a: diario de Dex, capítulo 4. A3.6a: admisión de Nurse Gwei (pruebas en el buzón y cuestionario de negación); el resto se reescribe en A3.6f. Ver qa/README.md § Diario.

goals.text: Make the old computer print what it knows.
Follow the map into the mountains.
Get admitted to the clinic. As a patient.
Get the doctor to open the treatment room.

notes.text: The Ledger opened Adrian's vault on the CRT. There's a map to something called 'Patient Zero Clinic'.
Patient roster: 'PATIENT ZERO — STATUS: ESCAPED'. Escaped through what? The printer gave me a map.
Nurse Gwei only lets in patients. Proof of symptoms: insomnia, loss. Denial she tests herself.
Insomnia and loss on file. Now I have to pass a denial test. I've been training my whole life.
Admitted. Diagnosis: textbook. I have a wristband. Mum would be so proud.
Satoshi only opens the treatment room to group therapy graduates. Chad runs the group. Downstairs, behind the patient records.
Satoshi authorized the treatment room. The door also has a physical keyhole. Dual lock.

hints: The basement computer has more to say. Feed it.
The chip from the dead rack. Adrian's Ledger. The floppy. In that order.
Use the burned chip, then the Ledger, then the floppy disk on the basement computer.
The printout is a map. Maps are for walking.
Out the front door. The far left of the yard.
Leave the house by the path on the far left.
Clinics want proof. You have symptoms. Find them in a form a slot can scan.
Insomnia comes in cans. Loss comes in crumpled notes. The clinic bin has both.
Pick up the note from the clinic trash can, then use a can and the note on the visitor box.
She's testing denial. So don't be honest. Be in denial.
Honest fails. Lying fails. Believe your own nonsense.
Buzz the intercom and say you can stop whenever you want. You just don't want to.
The doctor guards the treatment room. Doctors like paperwork.
Paperwork with Patient Zero's name on it. Sealed, ideally.
Give Satoshi the confidential envelope. Talk to him about the documents.

anonIdle: Fresh air. Use it. Don't use me.
